checklist.detail: Ragged Edge (ragged-edge.com) is not a tracked brand

problems.why: Both mentions use Ragged Edge as a studio example, but the homepage belongs to Ragged Edge Resort & Marina in the Florida Keys, not the studio.

problems.words: Lifestyle photography is rising across all sectors
problems.why: This can read as a rise in every sector, but the rise is for the tracked homepages taken together, and the story reports a decline in dev tools.
Both count bullets use internal shorthand for homepages whose imagery was assessed by AI.
Neither momentum figure tells readers whether the points measure a change in the share of homepages or a change in how fast that share is moving.

checklist.detail: the deck dates 14 Nov, 20 Nov are not in How we know (“Our read of the imagery, an AI estimate.”)
3 AI-read changes with no measured change beside them

problems.words: Three brands moved to corporate polish
problems.why: “Corporate polish” is slug’s label for a look, but the story never tells readers what visual feature the three homepages now share.
Readers cannot tell whether the 13.5% share is falling by 0.3 percentage points per quarter or whether “momentum” measures something else.
All four entries repeat the body almost word for word, so readers get the same rundown twice.

checklist.detail: a quiet change needs its before and after picture
the deck dates 6 Nov, 21 Nov are not in How we know (“Measured from captures on 13 and 20 November.”)

one accent colour on one page is a line on the tape, not a story. (a quiet change needs a confirmed new site icon, a confirmed new social card, or a confirmed change of headline or body typeface on another page at the same address)

problems.why: The change record says “Vivid pink,” but the measured facts line says “Before: Vivid red,” so the records disagree about the original colour.
The body is empty, leaving a single accent-colour change on one page as the whole story.
